label: late original-phase inputs (t>=4) of certain letters (d,r,m,a,b,s,l,...) and <DEL>
explanation: Fires only during reading: original phase at t>=4 (78% of mass) and the <DEL> step (22%); it never fires in the copy phase and never at t<=2 (40 activations at t=3). Rate rises with position (orig_idx 8: 48%) and with L (L=9 holds 47% of mass; L<=4 is essentially silent). It is token-selective on the current input, preferring d, r, m, a, b, s, l (rate 10-13%, about 2x) and then i, k, w, y. It favors first occurrences (in_first=1 holds 88% of mass) and sequences whose first token is e, t, c, 3, v, u, n or j (about 2x). The strongest activations come on d/r/m inputs at t=7-8 just before <DEL>, in sequences starting with e/c/v. It looks like a distributed code mixing position, current token and first token, so no compact predicate is precise: late position plus the token set gets about 90% of mass recall at about 0.30 precision, and adding the first_tok condition raises precision only to about 0.5 while halving recall.
